newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Mock blockade to protest Taiwan-N.Korea waste deal.
newsitem.headline: Mock blockade to protest Taiwan-N.Korea waste deal.

text.p: South Korean activists braved high seas to stage a mock blockade on Friday to protest against Taiwan's plan to ship nuclear waste to North Korea, witnesses said.

Scores of environmentalists aboard a fishing boat and two rubber dinghies surrounded a 100-ton vessel with fake yellow waste barrels in the wind-swept sea off the western port of Inchon, the witnesses said.

Protesters with the larger vessel shouted anti-nuclear slogans and waved picket signs condemning Taiwan at the port before setting sail. Their ship, the target of the blockade, hoisted Taiwanese and North Korean flags.
South Korean environmental groups have urged Taiwan Power Co to abandon a January 11 contract to ship up to 200,000 barrels of radioactive waste to impoverished North Korea.
Taiwanese newspapers have said the utilities will pay $1,150 per barrel to the communist state for the shipment.
"We know Taiwan will move the waste in June. We will try to prevent the shipment," said Choi Ye-young, an official from the Korean Federation for Enviornmental Movement.

On Monday the South Korean parliament adopted a declaration urging Taiwan to withdraw the plan. "We solemnly request that Taiwan or any other country refrain from sending nuclear waste to North Korea so that our offspring may enjoy a healthy and safe life," it said.
South Korea has said Taiwan's shipment could jeopardise relations between the countries, and Beijing has lashed out at Taipei for the plan.
Taiwan has said the deal is purely business and the Taipei-Pyongyang waste pact complies with all international regulations and shipments would be securely packed in steel barrels.
Taiwan has no diplomatic ties with either North Korea or South Korea, both of which recognise China.
